target_customer: HR and people leaders at growing companies, paying per employee
problem: Managers and HR teams ran performance reviews, goals and feedback in spreadsheets and disconnected tools.
business_model: B2B SaaS per employee per month
product_category: HR tech: performance management, goals and engagement

founders.name: Jack Altman
founders.background_notes: YC page lists Founder/CEO. Search summaries of Contrary Research say he came from Teespring, but I did not open that source.

founders.name: Eric Koslow
previous_startups: Multiple startups per YC bio (names not given)
founders.background_notes: YC bio mentions SaaS, video, streaming and doing business in Japan.

technical_complexity.rationale: Performance reviews and OKR tracking are standard web application work with integrations; no research-grade problem.

defensibility.rationale: Review history and goals data build up inside the tool and HR buyers rarely switch mid cycle, but the feature set is widely copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: HRIS vendors added performance modules over time; Lattice integrates with Workday and BambooHR today and kept growing.

market_need_then: Annual reviews were widely disliked and companies moved toward continuous feedback; Lattice launched its performance review product in October 2016 per its blog, after seeding with an OKR product (per a Contrary Research summary seen in search).

branding.domain_note: Now uses lattice.com; the earlier domain was not found.

identity.logo: Symbol called the Nest plus a logotype, per brand guidelines (search summary)
identity.voice_and_tone: People first: 'The HR platform that people love'

branding.brand_signature: People first tagline and green Nest symbol
branding.community_and_virality: Lattice runs a community for HR professionals and ranked #2 on the 2022 Great Place to Work and Fortune Best Medium Workplaces in Technology list.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong customer review volume and a recognizable HR brand, but the name is a common word and the 2024 AI worker backlash showed brand risk; no evidence the name itself drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Lattice grew from a YC W16 OKR and review tool into a unicorn, reaching a reported $3B valuation in January 2022 with $175M raised and a stated total near $330M. It cut about 15% of staff in January 2023 and in July 2024 dropped a plan to treat AI agents as employees after backlash. It is still independent and active under CEO Sarah Franklin, with strong investor backing and a large HR software market.
notes: Series B, C and D from the company's own blog titles plus search summaries; the Series C date was not seen so it is null (the $200M valuation is a TechCrunch figure seen in a search summary). Series E and F labels were not stated by an article I opened, so stage is other. No seed or Series A was found with amounts; one search summary says a $6.5M seed led by Thrive and a $1M pre-seed in 2015 (unverified), and Contrary Research says Series A came in 2017. Totals cited: $330M after Series F. Koslow left his CTO role in May 2022 and Sarah Franklin became CEO (search summaries). Competitor list empty: all competitor pages found were 2026 vendor comparisons, none dated near 2016. Layoffs of about 15% in January 2023 per search summary. Name origin not found.
